Sources: Dhaka Tribune

item.description:
Image: The Guardian

Sources: The Guardian, The Daily Star

In Bangladesh, banned Awami League members loot and burn properties in Gopalganj District, including BNP MP Md. Selimuzzaman Mollah's ancestral home, a police station, and a Grameen Bank branch, and vandalise BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami properties. Separately, attackers burn the homes of former politicians Rahim Ullah in Feni District, Shahriar Alam in Rajshahi District and Mahmud Hasan Sumon in Mymensingh District.

item.description:
Image: The Business Standard

In Kafrul, Dhaka, police fire around ten stun grenades against demonstrating garment workers following clashes with Bangladesh Nationalist Party activists who allegedly harassed female factory employees, causing workers to stage demonstrations and halt production at several nearby garment factories.

Sources: The Business Standard

In Gazipur, Savar, and Ashulia, Bangladesh, thousands of garment workers demanding a monthly minimum wage increase from ৳12,500 (US$100) to ৳30,000 ($240) block the Dhaka–Mymensingh Highway and set fire to a police vehicle, causing police to fire tear gas and stun grenades in Gazipur and Ashulia as 55 factories close across the three areas, while police report around 300 arrests across 24 cases filed in Savar and Ashulia during the protests.

Sources: The Daily Star

item.title: Aftermath of the July Uprising: In Gopalganj District, armed members of the banned Awami League, Chhatra League, and Jubo League detonate crude bombs and set fire to a private clinic owned by BNP Member of Parliament K M Babar of… / A crowd led by Chatra Dal members storms and sets fire to the residence of former Awami League Member of Parliament Shamim Osman in Narayanganj District, while unidentified attackers loot and set… / Two Bangladesh Nationalist Party members are killed when suspected members of the banned Awami League attack a motorcycle procession in Narail District, Bangladesh.
item.description:
Image: Views Bangladesh

In Gopalganj District, armed members of the banned Awami League, Chhatra League, and Jubo League detonate crude bombs and set fire to a private clinic owned by BNP Member of Parliament K M Babar of Gopalganj-2, forcing patients to evacuate. Attackers also burn at least five BNP offices across Muksudpur and Kashiani and target two Grameen Bank branches.

Sources: Dhaka Tribune

A crowd led by Chatra Dal members storms and sets fire to the residence of former Awami League Member of Parliament Shamim Osman in Narayanganj District, while unidentified attackers loot and set fire to two houses belonging to former Minister of Fisheries and Livestock SM Rezaul Karim in Pirojpur District. Separately, arsonists burn the residence of former Minister of Foreign Affairs Dipu Moni in Chandpur, and a crowd in Sirajganj vandalises the local Awami League office and the residence of former MP Habibe Millat.

Sources: Views Bangladesh, The Daily Star, The Daily Star

Two Bangladesh Nationalist Party members are killed when suspected members of the banned Awami League attack a motorcycle procession in Narail District, Bangladesh.

Sources: Daily Sun

item.title: Crimea attacks: The Crimean Bridge is struck by Ukrainian drones for the second day in a row, killing two people and prompting Russian authorities to close vehicle traffic again.
item.description:
The Crimean Bridge is struck by Ukrainian drones for the second day in a row, killing two people and prompting Russian authorities to close vehicle traffic again. Open-source intelligence report that a section of the road bridge damaged yesterday has collapsed into the Kerch Strait.

Sources: Reuters, Türkiye Today

Topics: Russo-Ukrainian war › Crimea attacks

item.title: Canada–China relations: Canada and China agree to further tariff reductions following talks between Canadian prime minister Mark Carney and Chinese leader Xi Jinping before the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
item.description:
Canada and China agree to further tariff reductions following talks between Canadian prime minister Mark Carney and Chinese leader Xi Jinping before the APEC summit in Shenzhen. China reduces tariffs on C$400 million (¥1.8 billion) in Canadian exports, while Canada extends relief for Chinese steel and aluminium.

Sources: AFP

Topics: Canada–China relations
